subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which dietary rule applies to a person following Islam (a Muslim)?
options: They eat only halal meat and avoid pork
They avoid beef because the cow is sacred
They follow a kosher diet avoiding shellfish
They eat only ital food with no additives
questions.explain: Muslims eat halal (permitted) foods and avoid pork and alcohol, which are haram (forbidden).

questions.q: A kosher diet, followed by many Jewish people, forbids which of these foods?
options: Pork and shellfish
Beef and lamb
All dairy products
Wheat and gluten
questions.explain: Kosher rules forbid pork and shellfish and do not allow meat and dairy to be eaten together.

questions.q: In a triangle test, a taster is given three samples and asked to:
options: identify the one sample that is different from the other two
rank all three samples in order of preference
score each sample on a scale of 1 to 5
state which single sample they most prefer
questions.explain: A triangle test presents three samples, two identical and one different, to detect whether a difference can be perceived.

questions.q: How many allergens must, by law, be highlighted on UK food labels?
questions.explain: UK law requires 14 named allergens (such as milk, eggs, peanuts and gluten) to be emphasised on labels.

questions.q: On a food label, the ingredients must be listed:
options: in descending order of weight, heaviest first
in alphabetical order
in ascending order of weight, lightest first
in order of nutritional value
questions.explain: By law, ingredients are listed in descending order of weight so the main ingredient appears first.

questions.q: A 'use by' date on a food product indicates:
options: the date after which the food may be unsafe to eat
the date after which the food loses quality but stays safe
the recommended date to display the product for sale
the date on which the food was manufactured
questions.explain: 'Use by' dates are about food safety and appear on high-risk foods that could cause illness if eaten late.

questions.q: Which dish is a traditional British cuisine dish?
options: Fish and chips
Paella
Sushi
Tagine
questions.explain: Fish and chips is a traditional British dish, whereas paella, sushi and tagine are from Spain, Japan and North Africa.

questions.q: On traffic light nutrition labelling, a red colour shows that the food is:
options: high in that nutrient
low in that nutrient
medium in that nutrient
free from that nutrient
questions.explain: Traffic light labels use red for high, amber for medium and green for low amounts of fat, saturated fat, sugars and salt.

questions.q: Why must a person with coeliac disease avoid foods such as bread, pasta and cous cous made from wheat?
options: They contain gluten, which damages the gut lining in coeliac disease
They contain lactose, which they cannot digest
They are too high in saturated fat
They naturally contain nuts
questions.explain: Coeliac disease is triggered by gluten found in wheat, barley and rye, so gluten-containing foods must be avoided.

questions.q: Many Hindus do not eat beef because:
options: the cow is considered sacred in Hinduism
beef is not permitted under halal rules
beef is forbidden by kosher law
beef always contains gluten
questions.explain: The cow is regarded as sacred in Hinduism, so many Hindus avoid beef.

questions.q: Why are samples in a sensory test given random three-digit codes and served in identical containers?
options: to reduce bias so tasters judge only the food itself
to make the test quicker to carry out
to increase the sweetness of the samples
to keep the samples at the correct temperature
questions.explain: Controlled conditions such as random codes and identical containers reduce bias so results are more reliable and valid.

questions.q: A 'best before' date differs from a 'use by' date because it refers to:
options: food quality rather than food safety
food safety rather than food quality
the manufacture date only
the sell-by display date only
questions.explain: 'Best before' relates to quality; food may still be safe to eat afterwards, unlike a 'use by' date.

questions.q: Which combination of ingredients best reflects traditional Italian cuisine?
options: Pasta, olive oil and tomatoes
Rice, soy sauce and noodles
Tortillas, beans and chilli
Rye bread, herring and dill
questions.explain: Italian cuisine typically features pasta, olive oil and tomatoes, unlike Chinese, Mexican or Scandinavian dishes.

questions.q: Choosing locally produced, seasonal food can reduce a consumer's environmental impact mainly by:
options: reducing food miles and transport emissions
increasing the fat content of the diet
removing the need for food labelling
extending the product's use by date
questions.explain: Local, seasonal food travels shorter distances, lowering food miles and the emissions from transporting it.

questions.q: A star profile (star diagram) is used in sensory analysis to:
options: plot and compare several sensory attributes of a product on one chart
identify the odd sample out of three
measure the exact weight of ingredients
record the product's use by date
questions.explain: A star profile plots attributes such as taste, texture and appearance on axes, allowing products to be compared visually.

questions.q: The reference intake (RI) for energy for an average adult, shown on food labels, is:
options: 2000 kcal per day
1500 kcal per day
2500 kcal per day
3000 kcal per day
questions.explain: Labels use a reference intake of 2000 kcal per day to help consumers judge how a portion fits into their diet.

questions.q: A customer is lactose intolerant. Which dessert would be most suitable for them?
options: A fruit sorbet made with water and fruit
A milk-based rice pudding
A cheesecake with a cream topping
An ice cream sundae
questions.explain: A water-and-fruit sorbet contains no milk sugar (lactose), unlike the dairy-based desserts.

questions.q: A cook has developed two versions of a soup and wants to find out which one people prefer. Which sensory test is most appropriate?
options: A paired preference test
A triangle test
A star profile alone
A ranking test of five samples
questions.explain: A paired preference test asks tasters to choose which of two samples they prefer, exactly what is needed here.

questions.q: A recipe contains wheat flour and eggs. On the packaged product's ingredients list, how must these allergens be presented?
options: emphasised, for example in bold, within the ingredients list
listed only in a separate 'may contain' box
shown only in the traffic light panel
left off the label because they are common ingredients
questions.explain: The 14 named allergens must be emphasised (e.g. in bold) within the ingredients list so consumers can spot them.

questions.q: A restaurant wants an autumn menu using seasonal British produce. Which ingredient best fits this aim?
options: Pumpkin and apples
Fresh strawberries and asparagus
Imported fresh mangoes
Tinned peaches
questions.explain: Pumpkin and apples are in season in British autumn, whereas strawberries and asparagus are spring and summer produce.
